authors: Røkås T.; Gómez-Baggethun E.
title: Defining a safe and just operating space for the Norwegian economy
variable_description: The remaining cumulative greenhouse gas emissions (excluding land cover changes) for a 50 % chance to stay below 1.5 °C by 2055 compared with pre-industrial level
variable_extra_description: CO2 budget adopted for Norway is an equal (per capita) share of the predicted world population between 1990 and 2055 (Statistics Norway; UN, 2019), accounting for accumulated emissions from 1990 to 2019 (Gütschow et al., 2021) and a carbon budget for a 50 % chance of staying within temperature rise of 1.5 °C equal to 500Gt CO2 (IPCC, 2021).
data_reference: Eora MRIO; IPCC, 2021; PRIMAP; Statistics Norway; United Nations, 2019
observations: To measure emissions, we used consumption-based accounts (CBA) (Lenzen et al., 2012, Lenzen et al., 2013). inter- and intra-generational sharing principle (Dao et al., 2018)

authors: Røkås T.; Gómez-Baggethun E.

variable_extra_description: CO2 budget adopted for Norway is an equal (per capita) share of the predicted world population between 1990 and 2055 (Statistics Norway; UN, 2019), accounting for accumulated emissions from 1990 to 2019 (Gütschow et al., 2021) and a carbon budget for a 50 % chance of staying within temperature rise of 1.5 °C equal to 500Gt CO2 (IPCC, 2021).

authors: O'Neill D.W.; Fanning A.L.; Lamb W.F.; Steinberger J.K.
title: A good life for all within planetary boundaries
variable_description: Consumption-based allocation of CO2 emissions from energy and cement production.
variable_extra_description: As an alternative boundary to 350 ppm, authors used the 2 C temperature stabilisation goal emphasised in the Paris Agreement. The cumulative emissions from 2011 to 2100 associated with a “high” probability (66%) of achieving this goal are approximately 1000 Gt CO2, or given a population of 7 billion people, approximately 1.61 t CO2 per capita (assuming CO2 emissions available in the 2011– 2100 carbon budget are distributed uniformly over time).

variable_extra_description: As an alternative boundary to 350 ppm, authors used the 2 C temperature stabilisation goal emphasised in the Paris Agreement. The cumulative emissions from 2011 to 2100 associated with a “high” probability (66%) of achieving this goal are approximately 1000 Gt CO2, or given a population of 7 billion people, approximately 1.61 t CO2 per capita (assuming CO2 emissions available in the 2011– 2100 carbon budget are distributed uniformly over time).

allocation_method: The global limit is computed first and then downscaled to compute the Swiss limit. Global and Swiss limits are expressed in terms of yearly values corresponding to a theoretically acceptable share of anthropised land cover. The global and Swiss limits are constant over the years but the per capita values evolve according to population size. The global limit per capita represents an equal share perspective.
variable_description: The selected indicator focuses on the anthropised surface. This indicator has been preferred to forested areas, because better data is available and the anthropised surface can be linked to human activities, enabling thus the computation of footprints.

authors: Priyadarshini P.; Abhilash P.C.
title: Exploring the â€˜Safe Operating Spaceâ€™ of India for the implementation of UN-Sustainable Development Goals through effectual policy alignment
control_variable: Ice free land converted to cropland
variable_description: NA
global_limit_considered: The planetary boundary proposed for assessment of land use change is the percentage of global land cover converted to cropland with the boundary set as ‘maximum of 15% of ice free land being used for crops.’ On the other hand, Steffen et al. (2015) defined land system change as the amount of forest cover remaining. The boundary is set differently depending on the forest biome (tropical, temperate, boreal) but works out to be maintaining ‘a minimum of 75% of global original forest cover.’ India, on its part has been performing well in terms of forest area cover and has witnessed an increasing trend in forest cover through formulation of schemes such as the National Agroforestry Mission and the Umbrella Scheme for Environment, Forestry and Wildlife.
observations: selection of land area under forest cover as the indicator for assessing land use change did not bring forth the challenges associated with this dimension. On the other hand, land use in India has been witnessing several changes with land area under agriculture witnessing an increasing trend with barren, fallow and uncultivated land declining. Therefore, ice free land converted to cropland was taken as the indicator owing to its relatedness with the agriculture sector and linkages with several targets of SDG 2 (zero hunger and sustainable agriculture)

observations: Considering the difficulty to set a limit for biodiversity based on well-accepted scientific evidence, an approach based on policy targets has been adopted, using the Aichi Biodiversity Targets of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). Three targets related to land cover (under Strategic Goal B and C)44 were selected: 1. ""Target 5: By 2020, the rate of loss of all natural habitats, including forests, is at least halved and where feasible brought close to zero, and degradation and fragmentation is significantly reduced"". 2. ""Target 7: By 2020 areas under agriculture, aquaculture and forestry are managed sustainably, ensuring conservation of biodiversity"". 3.  ""Target 15: By 2020, ecosystem resilience and the contribution of biodiversity to carbon stocks has been enhanced, through conservation and restoration, including restoration of at least 15 per cent of degraded ecosystems, thereby contributing to climate change mitigation and adaptation and to combating desertification.""
